patterns.title: Function Integration

children.title: Function Transfer
children.selection_condition: An existing part takes over a useful job from a dedicated part that can then be removed.

patterns.summary: Combine compatible functions in one component while preserving the conditions each job needs.

identity_resolution.decision: New engineering parent strategy. Function Transfer is its one direct specialization; the family is navigation, not a parent.
identity_resolution.boundary: Compatibility-based allocation of multiple roles to one component. Physical segmentation and independent renewal are different decisions. Architecture shading discusses its own envelope consequences, not a general function-integration strategy. The supplied substitutions also instantiate the narrower Function Transfer case; this article teaches parent-level compatibility and tradeoffs rather than authoring a separate child article.

use_when: Nearby components perform compatible jobs but add fastening or alignment work.
An existing housing or casting can take on another suitable role.
A proposed part reduction can be checked against manufacturing, operating, and renewal requirements.
goals: Reduce unnecessary part and assembly interfaces
Make shared material, load, and service conditions explicit
mechanisms: Allocate compatible functions to one component
Use local geometry to fulfill distinct roles
Remove unnecessary attachments and dedicated parts where justified
not_ideal_when: Functions require incompatible conditions or materials.
A wear feature needs independent renewal.
Extra tooling, access, or failure consequences outweigh the removed interfaces.
example_user_queries: We use a separate clamp even though the enclosure wall is right beside the cable.
Can we remove some small fastening operations from this instrument assembly?
Should this housing also provide the mounting support?
Our parts count is lower but the mold has become much more complicated.
A worn cable clip makes us replace an otherwise sound enclosure.
How do we know whether two jobs can share the same part?
The enclosure needs to be stiff but the retaining arm needs to flex.
Could the pump casting replace the bracket attached beneath it?
We want fewer parts without making repair more expensive.
Does getting rid of the clamp also get rid of the cable-retention job?
How should we choose between an integral clip and a replaceable insert?
One insertion works but the clip must survive repeated cable changes.

related_patterns.title: Functional Separation
related_patterns.relationship: Neighbor assigns incompatible functions to distinct elements; can coexist with integration at another boundary.

related_patterns.title: Function Transfer
related_patterns.relationship: Direct child for an existing part assuming a retained job from a removed dedicated part.

related_patterns.title: Eliminate a Supporting Task
related_patterns.relationship: Removes the reason for the job; integration can retain the job while changing who performs it.

related_patterns.title: Replaceable Wear Units
related_patterns.relationship: Provides a separate renewable wear element when local deterioration makes whole-component renewal unsuitable. Not a child of integration.

worked_examples.name: Instrument enclosure with molded cable-retaining arms
worked_examples.baseline: Enclosure, separate clamp, and two screws retain an internal cable on its route.
worked_examples.intervention: Two molded arms continuous with the wall provide cable retention.
worked_examples.selection_note: Also a Function Transfer case: the wall takes over the removed clamp’s retained job.
worked_examples.limits: Nominal geometric fixture only. Excludes cable and unrelated components from both inventories. No tolerances, jacket compression, arm strain, insertion force, durability, axial strain relief, sealing, time saving, or tool-cost prediction.

worked_examples.name: Pump casing with integral supporting foot
worked_examples.baseline: Separate mounting bracket attached to a fluid-containing housing.
worked_examples.intervention: Cast the supporting role into the housing and remove the bracket-to-housing interface.
worked_examples.evidence: Continuous casting and qualitative supporting load paths are visible; base fasteners remain.
worked_examples.selection_note: Also a Function Transfer case; parent discussion focuses on compatibility of containment and support.
worked_examples.limits: No casting dimensions, stress field, pressure rating, load capacity, mass or cost saving. Integration does not permit arbitrary nozzle or pipe loads.

worked_examples.name: Worn integral clip compared with renewable insert
worked_examples.baseline: Local lip wear defeats required retention while enclosure remains otherwise sound; assumed service policy has no local repair.
worked_examples.intervention: Provide a separately supported and retained service insert with a usable withdrawal route.
worked_examples.evidence: Renewal scope changes from whole enclosure to insert, with an explicit extra service interface.
worked_examples.limits: Wear is schematic and enlarged; no measured wear, failure cycle, renewal threshold, service interval, cost, or maintenance time. An insert is a design candidate, not a universal repair; integrated durability may be acceptable in another duty.

graphics.decision: Three static original SVG diagrams and three phone companions; no widget.
graphics.reason: Matched component boundaries, one continuous casting, and a renewal-scope comparison make the decisions inspectable without a simulation. The numerical fixture is elementary passage geometry, not a material model suitable for arbitrary sliders.
graphics.style: Approved fixed-white editorial engineering drawings with regular Helvetica Neue, fine neutral lines, and restrained green.

figures.learning_question: What parts and assembly tasks can be removed when the wall also retains the cable?
figures.changed: Separate clamp and two screws replaced by molded arms continuous with the enclosure wall.
figures.arrow_meaning: No motion or force arrows; thin ticked lines mark nominal throat width.
figures.phone_composition: Matched sections remain stacked, with larger labels and greater spacing before the second detail.
figures.alt: Matched enclosure sections compare a separate clamp secured with two screws against retaining arms molded into the wall. The same cable is shown in both; the integral detail labels a 5 mm throat and a 6 mm cable diameter.
figures.caption: Original schematic sections with illustrative nominal dimensions. The selected subassembly changes from enclosure, clamp, and two screws to one enclosure. A rigid 6 mm circular cable section requires the 5 mm throat to widen by at least 1 mm for passage; equal arm movement would be 0.5 mm each. This geometry does not establish insertion force, strain, durability, or axial strain relief.

figures.learning_question: How can one casting provide both containment and support?
figures.changed: An integral supporting foot removes a dedicated bracket and its housing attachment; base fasteners remain.
figures.arrow_meaning: Qualitative load-transfer paths, not a free-body force balance or computed stress.
figures.phone_composition: One full-width section retained; labels below the drawing are spaced farther apart vertically.
figures.alt: Section through a hollow pump housing shows its lower wall continuing into an integral supporting foot bolted to a base. Green arrows trace the qualitative transfer of housing loads through the continuous casting to its mounting foot.
figures.caption: Original schematic, not to scale. The housing now provides fluid containment and support through one casting. Arrows indicate qualitative load-transfer paths, not calculated forces or a stress field. Base fasteners remain. No pressure rating, support capacity, or casting dimensions are established.

figures.learning_question: Which element must be renewed after local clip wear?
figures.changed: Whole-enclosure renewal under the assumed no-local-repair policy compared with a separately renewable retaining insert.
figures.arrow_meaning: Upward arrow means insert withdrawal after release; green identifies the renewed element.
figures.phone_composition: Both sections stay stacked; larger labels and a larger interval separate the two renewal arrangements.
figures.alt: Stacked enclosure sections compare a worn integral retaining lip, whose renewal includes the enclosure, with a separate retaining insert lifted from its supported seat. Green identifies the element renewed in each arrangement.
figures.caption: Illustrative renewal-scope comparison. In the upper case, an assumed service policy provides no local repair for the worn integral feature. Below, the insert is a separately retained service part; the arrow shows withdrawal motion after release. Wear is schematic and enlarged. No wear rate, service interval, or maintenance-time gain is predicted.

graphics.provenance: Original editable schematic geometry. No traced manufacturer/book illustrations, external photographs, generated raster imagery, or computed-looking stress fields.
